hints.content:
$\displaystyle \lim_{x\to -7}f(x)$ represents the limit of $f$ as $x$ approaches $-7$.

Let's look at the table and see if the $f(x)$-values seem to approach a distinct finite value as the $x$-values approach $-7$.

$x$ | $f(x)$
-: | :- 
$-7.1$| $4.37$
$-7.01$| $4.18$
$-7.001$| $4.01$

As the $x$-values *increase towards* $x=-7$ (i.e. approach it from the left), the $f(x)$-values seem to approach $4$.

$x$ | $f(x)$
-: | :-
$-6.999$| $-4.01$
$-6.99$| $-4.18$
$-6.9$| $-4.37$

As the $x$-values *decrease towards* $x=-7$ (i.e. approach it from the right), the $f(x)$-values seem to approach $-4$.
The function doesn't seem to approach the same value from both sides, so the limit doesn't exist.

question.content:
The function $f$ is defined over the real numbers. This table gives a few values of $f$.

$x$ | $f(x)$
-: | :-
$-7.1$| $4.37$
$-7.01$| $4.18$
$-7.001$| $4.01$
$-6.999$| $-4.01$
$-6.99$| $-4.18$
$-6.9$| $-4.37$

**What is a reasonable estimate for $\displaystyle \lim_{x\to -7}f(x)$?**
